name: What is the difference between partial and full pool removal?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between partial pool removal and full pool removal, and which one is better for a Los Angeles home?
mainEntity.text: What is the difference between partial pool removal and full pool removal, and which one is better for a Los Angeles home?

acceptedAnswer.text: Partial and full pool removal solve different problems. Partial removal, often called fill-in, is usually the lower-cost option and works well when the goal is simply to reclaim the space for lawn or landscaping. Full removal takes out more of the shell and debris, then backfills the cavity, which usually costs more and takes longer. Full removal is the better choice when a homeowner wants maximum flexibility for future additions, heavy landscaping, or site work where a buried shell could become a problem. In dense Los Angeles neighborhoods, many owners choose based on future plans for the yard and resale concerns. Before deciding, ask whether the contractor includes compacted engineered fill, how settlement is handled, and whether future building over the area is allowed. The right option depends on budget, access, and long-term use of the property.
acceptedAnswer.description: Partial pool removal breaks up part of the shell, fills the cavity with compacted soil, and leaves some buried structure in place. Full pool removal removes most or all of the shell before backfilling. Partial removal is usually cheaper and faster, while full removal gives more flexibility for future construction and reduces the chance of hidden settlement issues.
